name: Detect Cycle (Floyd's)
description: Floyd's tortoise-and-hare algorithm: uses two pointers moving at different speeds to detect cycles in O(n) time and O(1) space.
aim: Detect if a linked list has a cycle using two pointers — slow moves one step, fast moves two steps. If they ever meet, a cycle exists.
howItWorks: While fast and fast.next are not null:
If fast reaches null: NO CYCLE
To find entry: reset slow to head, advance both one step at a time

time.bestCase: Cycle detected or no cycle found early

realWorld: Detecting infinite loops in state machines
Finding duplicate numbers in O(1) space (array-as-linked-list)
Detecting loops in filesystem directory structure
whenToUse: When hashing visited nodes is too costly
alternatives: Hash Set — store visited nodes, O(n) space but simpler
Brent's algorithm — variant with slightly better constants

inputHint: The LAST number is the index the tail links back to; use 99 for no cycle.
